The published five-run receipt for the FUSED measurement shows the same property at the aggregation level: five different backend identities, five different receipt digests, one tokenwise-KLD digest 52e35723..., population_stddev_of_run_means 0.0.

disclosures.detail: Inherited from the final25 panel: role separation only, no published lexical or n-gram scan.

Captured on the streaming lane. Routed-expert combine order differs from the sealed EP8 lane. The measured bridge is delta_mean_kld -8.4958e-06 with max_abs_per_window_delta 2.8735e-04 over 25 windows, and tokenwise_kld_sha256_matches_sealed is false: streaming runs are bitwise identical to each other but NOT to sealed-lane runs. A comparison against a sealed-ep8 capture is cross-lane and may never be cited as a floor.

The published K6 materialization receipt names a packed_root that no longer exists (/home/jl_fs/glm53-k6/out-k6). That path is stripped from the copy in upstream/ and recorded in stripped_fields; it is not needed to read this dataset.

equality_receipt.claim: head_equal and final_norm_equal between the zai BF16 and FP8 releases; both file digests are 47eaf729... and c228a123...

head.note: TR3 keeps the head native: quantization_config.head_bits is 16 and lm_head.weight appears as a plain BF16 [154880, 4096] tensor in the published index (verified by range-reading the shard header), NOT as a trellis/suh/svh/mcg group. Its content digest therefore equals the reference head's, which is what makes a shared-head comparison against the root LEGAL here. A stock-EXL3 artifact with head_bits 6 would carry a DIFFERENT digest and the comparator would refuse (HEAD-1b).

divergences.reason: every capture declares its OWN head identity by tensor content digest; the comparator refuses a hidden-form comparison across differing heads. kimi-k3 applies one --lm-head to both sides and records no per-capture head.
lane is required and gated at compare time so registry BIAS-006 is checked before a number exists, not at submission.
scoring_window is part of panel identity, not a comparator flag: a score_from=1024 number is a different panel, not a variant.
self-compare is a first-class mode asserting exactly 0.0; nobody else has one.
required, fp64 default; an fp32 estimator lands in a different comparability class on the same data and that must be visible.
declared vs present record counts with shard_of; fixes our own manifest that claimed 5,120 captures in a 512-file repository.
the panel is a separately referenceable object, which is what makes a candidate capture publishable standalone.
lets a llama.cpp .kld (uint16 log-probs, max_logit-16 clamp) be ingested without laundering a lossy capture as exact.
our packed and streaming lanes vary mask construction; a single-request-per-context capture path makes it invariant and has no equivalent field.
hidden form is the default; logit form must declare head_separable:false with a reason. 31.7 GB vs 419 MB on this panel.

interop.note: Publishing this capture is what the K6 data loss argues for: the packed reading paths (--source checkpoint, --source payload-store) are unreachable from public artifacts because materialization-receipt.json still names the dead /home/jl_fs/glm53-k6/out-k6, and only --source exl3hf still works. A published capture makes the reading path irrelevant.

contamination.method: role separation only; no lexical or n-gram scan published

scoring_window.policy: every prediction position of every window is scored; nothing is dropped

covers: every published file except checksums.txt and fidelity-dataset.json, via checksums.txt
fidelity-dataset.json itself, via the self-blanked seal
every capture tensor a second time by CONTENT, via capture.capture_content_digest
